description: A copy read from a copy behind at its old path, whose disk holds no folder at the file's new path, makes that folder with no model: 0755 whatever the umask, here the units' 0027, which left it 0750 and closed to a media server running under another account. Its event mkdir holds the mode 0755 and no owner.

steps.query: SELECT c.disk_id, CAST(f.lpath AS TEXT), CAST(c.old_lpath AS TEXT) FROM copies c JOIN files f ON f.id = c.file_id ORDER BY c.disk_id

steps.text:
pool_id = "p"
catalog = "${SANDBOX}/catalog.db"
[view]
mount = "${SANDBOX}/pool"
[defaults]
replicas = 2
[[disk]]
id = "t1"
uuid = "3f1c9a2e-5b7d-4c1e-9a0b-2d4f6e8a1c3b"
mount = "${SANDBOX}/disks/t1"
fs = "ext4"
[[disk]]
id = "t2"
uuid = "7a2b4c6d-8e0f-4a1b-9c2d-3e4f5a6b7c8d"
mount = "${SANDBOX}/disks/t2"
fs = "ext4"
[[disk]]
id = "t3"
uuid = "4f1c9a2e-5b7d-4c1e-9a0b-2d4f6e8a1c3b"
mount = "${SANDBOX}/disks/t3"
fs = "ext4"

steps.query: SELECT json_extract(data, '$.disk'), json_extract(data, '$.path'), json_extract(data, '$.mode'), json_type(data, '$.uid'), json_type(data, '$.gid') FROM events WHERE kind = 'mkdir'
SELECT kind, state FROM ops WHERE disk_id = 't3' ORDER BY id
SELECT CAST(lpath AS TEXT), mode, created_by FROM entries WHERE disk_id = 't3'
